marketOverview: Greenville and the Upstate have an active concrete-coating market serving homeowners, garages, patios, basements, workshops, retail spaces, warehouses, automotive shops, gyms, and commercial kitchens.

The dominant residential promise is a fast installation, often one day, using polyaspartic or polyurea systems with decorative flake finishes. Commercial competitors emphasize chemical resistance, slip resistance, reduced downtime, and systems selected for the use of the space.

Common competitor claims include diamond grinding, moisture testing, local ownership, free estimates, written warranties, and service across Greenville, Simpsonville, Mauldin, Greer, Taylors, Easley, Anderson, and Spartanburg. These claims should be independently verified before MGT repeats them.

The clearest opportunity is a professional, evidence-led brand that shows the actual slab condition, preparation method, coating system, cure requirements, final result, and warranty terms for each project instead of relying only on generic durability claims.

currentBusinessPlan: Stage 1 - Establish a professional flooring and concrete-coatings brand in Greenville, SC, with residential garage, basement, workshop, patio, and porch work as the initial revenue focus.

Stage 1 - Confirm the public-facing brand name, business registration, domain, insurance, supplier relationships, system specifications, warranty language, service radius, and qualified installation capabilities before making performance claims.

Stage 2 - Build a repeatable residential sales and delivery process: assessment, substrate and moisture review, written scope, preparation plan, coating selection, installation schedule, cure guidance, maintenance instructions, warranty documentation, review request, and project photography.

Stage 2 - Create a verified portfolio of local work and use it to support Google Business Profile, local organic search, referral partnerships, social video, paid search, and retargeting. Measure calls, form submissions, booked assessments, close rate, average project value, and source of lead.

Stage 3 - Expand into commercial and light-industrial flooring after residential proof, staffing, equipment, insurance, and supplier support are sufficient. Begin with well-defined spaces such as automotive shops, gyms, retail, offices, warehouses, and service businesses rather than claiming every industrial capability.

Stage 4 - Consider handyman and remodeling only as a separately positioned service division with its own scope, qualified trades, licenses, insurance, project proof, and information architecture. Keep the initial brand associated with flooring excellence rather than a generic list of home services.

Business risk - The MGT Services name has a local South Carolina naming collision in concrete coatings and handyman services. Complete legal, domain, social-handle, and Google Business Profile availability checks before investing in brand assets or advertising.
nextSteps: Confirm a distinctive public-facing brand name, domain, South Carolina business registration, trademark availability, insurance, coating-system supplier, and warranty terms before launch.

Launch residential garage, basement, patio, porch, and workshop pages first, supported by real photography, sample colors, preparation details, quote requirements, cure times, and verified service areas.

Build a documented project library. Each case study should identify the location at an appropriate privacy level, substrate condition, preparation, system, finish, installation dates, return-to-service guidance, final photography, and customer permission.

Add commercial pages after residential proof exists: automotive shops, warehouses, gyms, retail, offices, and food-service environments should explain performance requirements, downtime planning, safety, and maintenance.

Use Google Business Profile and local SEO as the foundation, then publish installation videos and educational short-form content to Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, and LinkedIn. Use paid search for high-intent quote terms and retargeting only after conversion tracking is reliable.

Treat handyman and remodeling as a later, separately organized service line with its own scope, qualifications, project proof, and landing pages. Do not dilute the initial flooring brand with an undifferentiated list of home services.
